items.title: The dependency-vetting check triggers on workflow action references
body: The security-hygiene.dependency-vetting deterministic trigger keys on package manifests only, so a diff adding googleapis/release-please-action@v5.0.0 — third-party code running with contents:write — showed 'not triggered' and the batch 11 T3 reviewer had to file the missing vetting record by hand.

Fix: extend the trigger — a diff that adds or changes a `uses:` reference under .github/workflows/ requires dependency_vetting with the workflow file in manifests and the action reference in dependencies. Requires the owner's ruling first: the check lives on a STANDING entry (both knowledge copies) and the runner change lives in crates/houserules/src/rules/audit.rs's `run_check` (batch 20 T3 retired template/tools/kb.mjs, the runner's pre-rewrite home).
Source: batch 11 branch review, violated_rules 2 and template_defects 2 (2026-09-03). Standing-entry change: OWNER RULING PENDING, listed in the batch 11 report.

Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (design.md 5.147, meta-spec O13): joins batch 35 (2.0.0, batch 3 of 5); the trigger change ships as a security-hygiene pack version through the runner port, and its standing-entry ruling is taken at the batch-35 spec review (D10).

items.title: Modular installs: adopters choose the feature set
body: Owner intent recorded at the Tier-2 CLI-surface ruling (2026-09-04): houserules becomes modular — an adopter can install only backlog management, or rules management without the backlog, or the full kit. This is WHY the flat command surface keeps per-module checks (check-knowledge, check-backlog) and the Rust crate separates rules, backlog, and install modules.

Shape: a feature/selection mechanism in init (and update honoring it) that installs a subset of the payload — the seeded files, generated artifacts, skills, and checks scoped to the chosen modules; the stamp records the selection. Details to the batch spec when gated, AFTER the Tier-2 port completes (the port ships everything; the crate boundaries prepare the split).
Source: owner, 2026-09-04, at the batch 15 CLI-surface ruling; the Tier-2 spec's architecture section carries the boundary design.
Owner ruling 2026-10-10 (batch-33 Q1, design.md 5.96): not in 2.0.0. It ships after 2.0.0 as a minor release under the 2.0 surface rule (D2).

Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (meta-spec O13, while it was asked): a backlog-only install, a tracker without the knowledge base, is out of scope; Beads serves that use, and it is no longer houserules' main focus. Owner, verbatim: "tracker without a knowledge base is no longer in scope. People can use beads for that. That is no longer houserules main focus."

Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (design.md 5.147, meta-spec O13): dropped. 2.0.0 delivers the in-scope parts through HR-180 (the rules without a backlog: no default tracker, 5.138), HR-182 (optional packs, 5.105), and HR-181 (an optional workflow, 5.111); the remaining part, a backlog-only install, is out of scope. This replaces Q1's 'ships after 2.0.0 as a minor' for this item.

items.title: Curated starter packs: docs style and code quality that adopters add
body: Owner intent (2026-09-04): adopters should start with a curated default set of rules — docs style and code-quality style in tag-pilot's vein — instead of a near-empty seed. Today template/knowledge/ ships 36 entries that are process-heavy (23 process entries) while quality carries 2 and writing-style 3; no docs-style or language-agnostic code-quality starter content exists.

Shape: curate a default entry set for the quality and writing-style topics (and a docs area if warranted), modeled on the tag-pilot checkout's rules as a READ-ONLY reference (houserules.tag-pilot-is-read-only). Content work, independent of the Tier-2 binary; interacts with HR-053 (a starter set is what a modular rules-only install would seed). Curation choices and any new areas go to the batch spec when gated.
Source: owner, 2026-09-04, mid batch 16.

Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (design.md 5.147, meta-spec O13): ships after 2.0.0 as a minor, rescoped to curated starter packs (for example docs style and code quality) that the binary carries and a project adds with pack add; the default stays the knowledge-base pack alone (issue 62), and an added pack is a minor change (D2).

items.title: kb audit: an explicit empty-range mode
body: Batch 16 branch review, template defect 2: T5's three empty-range audits (research task, no diff) produced three byte-identical near-vacuous files — every deterministic row passes trivially and none speaks to the actual deliverable; the schema still demands self_audit, so the ritual ran three times for no signal.

Change: give audit an explicit empty-range mode that says so in one summary row (it already emits empty_range: true), and let a research task's report point its evidence rows at the workspace doc instead of the diff. Source: batch 16 branch review retrospective, 2026-09-04.

items.title: Narrow check-report-claims' paste-run lint: quote-aware placeholder, $(...)-aware tokenizer
body: Batch 20 T2 fix round 1 review, important findings 3-4: the paste-run lint (HR-071) ships with two measured false-positive vehicles, both disclosed as Limits bullets in crates/houserules/src/report_claims.rs rather than narrowed. (1) The appended-annotation check's subshell exemption only covers a `(...)` wrapping the WHOLE command; a chained `cmd1 && (cmd2)` reads as an appended annotation instead — .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-04-batch-17/task-2-report.json live_run[8] is a real instance the shipped checker flags. (2) The placeholder check ignores quote_mask's state entirely, so a quoted angle-bracket literal that is command DATA (an HTML-comment probe, or a `Co-Authored-By: ... <email>` trailer this repository's own standing no-coauthor rule guarantees will keep generating) misreads as a placeholder — the lint's most frequent false positive at filing time: 5 instances across 4 workspace reports.

The narrowing: (a) a quote-aware placeholder arm in find_placeholder, skipping any span quote_mask already marks as inside a quoted string; (b) a $(...)-aware tokenizer arm in quote_mask, tracking that a same-character quote re-opened inside a `$(...)`/`` `...` `` command substitution starts a fresh, independent quoted region rather than closing the one around the whole substitution (the vehicle report_claims.rs's own Limits section discloses from batch 20 T2's first pass, 2 instances in that same review's own corpus sweep). Deferred per process.no-tech-debt: both are bounded, well-scoped engineering — quote_mask already carries the byte-level state the placeholder check would need to consult, and the $(...) arm needs a small quote-context stack, not a rewrite — not a correctness blocker for HR-071's shipped form, which already discloses both gaps with their measured instances rather than shipping them silently.

items.title: check-backlog gains a --fix arm for a non-round-tripping backlog file
body: Filed by the task-1 fix round 1 review (minor issue 8): check-backlog's round-trip finding (HR-076) names a concrete remedy per file class, but only backlog/items/*.json has a shipped command that can reach it (`houserules set`). The other five files (schema.json, amendments.json, batches.json, decisions.json, parked.json) have no writer at all, so an adopter who trips this on one of them is told to hand-reproduce serde_json's pretty-printer byte for byte.

Candidate: a `--fix` arm on check-backlog (or a small subcommand) that rewrites the named file through the same `crate::emit::emit` call the check already compares against, so the repair path and the check path stay the same function. Not built in the fix round that filed it: the message-only remedy was the scoped fix; a --fix arm is a larger surface (does it fix every diverging file in one run, or one named file? does it need a --dry-run?) that deserves its own task.
Owner ruling 2026-10-10 (batch-33 Q1, design.md 5.96): not in 2.0.0. It ships after 2.0.0 as a minor release under the 2.0 surface rule (D2).

items.title: Main needs the code owner's approval for everyone but the owner; Dependabot auto-merge runs on the owner's token
body: Owner ruling 2026-09-11: only the owner merges to main without an approval; every other contributor's PR needs the owner's approving review. Applied as a second ruleset `approval` on the default branch (one approving review, code-owner review required, stale reviews dismissed on push, threads resolved) whose only bypass actor is the repository admin role. The first ruleset `main` (the eight required checks incl. CodeQL, linear history, no force-push, PR required) keeps no bypass and binds the owner too. GitHub cannot exempt one rule inside a ruleset, hence the split.

Consequence and the ruled fix: GitHub refuses the Actions app as a bypass actor on a user-owned repository, so a merge enabled with GITHUB_TOKEN now waits for an approval and the HR-092 auto-merge stalls. The owner chose the token route: .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml enables auto-merge with a fine-grained personal access token of the owner (Contents and Pull requests read/write on this repository only), stored as the Dependabot secret DEPENDABOT_AUTOMERGE_TOKEN (a Dependabot-triggered workflow reads that store, not Actions secrets). A merge performed as the owner also starts the push workflows on main, which lifts HR-092's GITHUB_TOKEN limit for these merges.

PENDING proof: the next minor or patch Dependabot PR merging on its own with the workflow green. Flip to done with that PR's number. HR-068 (a token for the release flow) stays a separate ruling: release-please edits a workflow file, which needs the `workflows` permission this token does not carry.

Proof run, read 2026-10-01: negative. PR #31 (clap 4.6.6 to 4.6.7, a patch) got auto-merge enabled by the owner's token eleven seconds after it opened on 2026-09-18, then waited: it merged on 2026-09-21, seconds after the owner's own approving review. The token enables auto-merge; it does not satisfy the approval ruleset, because an enabled auto-merge waits for every requirement and the admin bypass does not apply to it. PRs #33 and #34 (github/codeql-action analyze and init, 4.38.0 to 4.38.1, opened 2026-09-25) stand blocked on two counts: the approving review is still required, and both CodeQL `analyze` jobs fail on each PR - Dependabot bumps the two actions in separate PRs, and they must share one version. PR #33 (analyze at 4.38.1) prints `Loaded a configuration file for version '4.38.0', but running version '4.38.1'`; PR #34 (init at 4.38.1) prints the same line with the two versions exchanged. PR #32 (dependabot/fetch-metadata 2.5.0 to 3.1.0, a major) is approved, carries no auto-merge by design, and is behind main.

Repair ruled 2026-10-01 (design.md 5.87): the workflow approves a minor or patch Dependabot PR with the owner's token before it enables auto-merge, and a Dependabot group moves the `github/codeql-action` pair in one PR. The item closes on the first minor or patch Dependabot PR that merges with no owner action.

Proof run 2, read 2026-10-02: the repair works as built, and the merge still waits. Dependabot closed PRs #33, #34, #44, and #45. It opened PR #48 (the `codeql-action` group, both steps in one PR) at 08:27:16 UTC, after batch 28 reached main. The workflow approved PR #48 with the owner's token at 08:27:26 and enabled auto-merge at 08:27:29. Every required check passed, both CodeQL `analyze` jobs included. The release commit of 1.2.0 reached main at 08:33:39, and the PR had not merged by then. The `main` ruleset requires an up-to-date branch (`strict_required_status_checks_policy: true`), so PR #48 is `BEHIND` and its auto-merge waits. HR-156 holds that stall and its fix. Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (design.md 5.89): nobody touches PR #48; it is the proof of HR-156. This item closes when PR #48, or a later minor or patch Dependabot PR, merges with no owner action.

PR #48 is no proof. The owner's account commented `@dependabot recreate` on PRs #48, #43, and #32 between 10:29:21 and 10:30:00 UTC on 2026-10-02. Dependabot recreated PR #48 at 10:31:56, and it merged at 10:39:38 with the approval and the auto-merge that the workflow had set, with no further act. That is a merge after an owner action. It does show the second half of the chain: once Dependabot brings its branch up to date, the PR merges on its own. This item closes on the next minor or patch Dependabot PR that merges with no owner action.

Proof run, 2026-10-10 (batch 30 merged to main as df1f228, fast-forward from the CLI after the owner stored DEPENDABOT_AUTOMERGE_TOKEN in the Actions store): the dependabot-rebase run on the push of df1f228 (run 38076665153) found PR #53 (jdx/mise-action 5.0.0 to 5.1.1, a minor update, auto-merge on, approved, 14 commits behind main) and commented `@dependabot rebase` with the owner's token at 18:39:39 UTC. Dependabot force-pushed the rebased head f43470a at 18:40:33. dependabot-auto-merge (run 38076739486) enabled auto-merge again at 18:40:43. Every check passed, and PR #53 merged at 18:48:36 as d80588c, twelve seconds after it read CLEAN, with no owner action; GitHub names the owner's account as the merger because the owner's token enabled the auto-merge. The dependabot-rebase run on that push (run 38077278382) printed 'No Dependabot pull request with auto-merge is behind main and free of failed checks.' PR #53 is the first minor or patch Dependabot PR that merged with no owner action: closed.

items.title: check-report-claims: HR-110's locative class ('the X live in Y')
body: Batch 25 T3a shipped only HR-110's number class ('N passed', 'N files' next to a cited capture); the locative class the same item names ('a report narrative stating the X live in Y, citing a retained capture, fails when Y is absent from that capture') is not implemented. The two real batch-23 locative instances that motivated HR-110 both sat in a commit body and a plan file, neither a report-narrative field check-report-claims scans, so this task's own corpus run (every retained deliverable in the tracked tree and the batch workspaces) turned up no report-narrative locative instance to derive a mechanical, low-noise trigger from.

Scoped out per quality.gates-derive-their-scope rather than shipped as a guess: a 'the X live in Y' sentence has no citation-adjacent signal as reliable as HR-110's own digit-token match, and this task's corpus run showed even the number class needs real instances to calibrate against (the 'N files (a, b, c)' enumeration-list false positive, fixed in the same task, only surfaced once real corpus data was run through it). Pick this up once a report-narrative locative instance exists to calibrate against, or once a design session derives a trigger some other way; do not ship an untested heuristic against it.

Rider (batch 25 branch review): report_claims.rs is 2889 lines - before this item (or HR-124) lands there, split the three checks and the shared resolver into submodules per the batch-25 plan's god-file direction.

items.title: check-report-claims: HR-111's multi-file sweep-coverage case
body: Batch 25 T3a fix round 1: check_narrative_sweep_coverage (HR-111) returns early unless a report's files_changed names exactly one file. Measured over the task's own 350-file corpus (t3a-files-changed-reach.py, retained at .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-14-batch-25/): 3 of 350 deliverables carry exactly one files_changed entry (where the check runs), 93 carry more than one, 3 carry an empty files_changed array, and the remaining 251 are review kinds that carry no files_changed field at all -- so the check is inert on 347 of 350 retained deliverables, the common case by a wide margin.

Blocker: this task's corpus run found no reliable signal for WHICH of several changed files a given sweep/enumeration citation is offered as proof for. Comparing a sweep's content against the WHOLE files_changed list once produced a flood of false positives (a narrowly-scoped sweep has no reason to mention a plan file or a schema copy the same task also edited); a two-citation-per-sentence heuristic (the sweep, then a second citation naming the certified file) would have missed the task's own real motivating instance (HR-111's own origin, batch 23 T1: the sentence names only the sweep, relying on the reader knowing which file the task is about). Picking this up needs either a design session to derive a real per-file attribution signal, or a corpus of real multi-file sweep citations large enough to calibrate one against -- this task's own corpus supplied none.
Origin: batch 25 T3a (HR-111); this item schedules the deferred multi-file case rather than leaving it only as a report concern, per process.no-tech-debt.
Rider (batch 25 branch review): see HR-123's split-first note - the same file hosts both items.

items.title: Reports re-open every file:line citation at HEAD; check-report-claims compares the cited line
body: GitHub issue #35 (owner, 2026-09-30). The issue reports from the adopter project orrery, batch 1: process.claims-match-artifacts failed in 7 of 13 tasks, and every failure was drift - a line number, a timestamp, a command string, or a count carried from a draft into the final report. Each failure cost a review round.

Request, two parts. (1) The closing act of the implementer template lists every file-and-line citation in the report after the last edit and re-opens each cited line at HEAD; it copies every command field from the shell history and never retypes a command. (2) check-report-claims resolves each <file>:<line> citation against the tree at HEAD and reports a line whose text differs from the fragment the report quotes.

Triage 2026-10-01: check-report-claims already resolves a citation's file and fails a line number past the end of the file (crates/houserules/src/report_claims.rs); it does not compare the cited line's text with a quoted fragment. Part 2 extends that check. Part 1 changes .claude/agents/implementer.md, so process.evals-rerun applies.

Batch 28 result (2026-10-01): part 1 shipped; part 2 did not. The owner ruled the checker rule heuristic and corpus-gated, with a bar of zero false positives (docs/specs/2026-10-01-batch-28-issue-batch.md, section HR-141; design.md 5.87 directs the batch but does not hold this ruling). The rule as specified (a backticked fragment of the citing sentence must occur in the cited line or range) was measured over the 166 retained deliverables of kind task-report. Hits, classified aged / true / false: as specified 52 = 12 / 2 / 38; fired only on drift evidence (a fragment occurs elsewhere in the cited file) 19 = 9 / 2 / 8; also limited to identifier-shaped fragments 12 = 5 / 2 / 5. At that narrowest trigger the fix-round finding and fix fields give 11 hits = 4 / 2 / 5 and the implemented and self_review fields give 1 hit = 1 / 0 / 0, so a field restriction reaches zero false hits only with zero true hits. Three of the twelve rows at the narrowest trigger are judgment calls, each marked with its alternative class in the classification: one counted true whose alternative is false, one counted false whose alternative is aged, and one counted false whose alternative is true. Taken the other way, they move the false count at that trigger between 3 and 6. The classification counts a hit aged only when the rule passes at a commit the report lists. Under that definition three false hits remain in every variant: a fragment that sits on an adjacent line, fragments that belong to sibling citations in the same sentence, and a fragment that names another job in the cited file. Under the wider definition (a hit is aged whenever the cited file changed after the report), the first of the three counts as aged and the other two remain. Typical false hits: a `grep -c` count such as `read_parity.rs:3` read as a line citation, and a sentence whose backticked token names a command or a neighbor, not code on the cited line. The rule is not wired. Open for a later spec: a trigger with better precision, or an owner ruling that accepts false hits. The module and its tests, unwired, are in the batch-28 workspace on the controller's machine (t5-evidence/wip/); the workspace is not tracked.

Notes for that later spec, from the batch-28 task: (a) a sentence boundary of `.`, `!`, or `?` plus whitespace splits wrongly at `...` inside a backtick span; (b) the classification rests on pre-aggregation commit states, most of them reachable from no ref, so a `git gc` can remove them and the corpus run must be repeated on states that still exist; (c) the tests of the two narrowed variants in the unwired module still expect the finding text of the unnarrowed rule.
Status after batch 28: partial. The template step shipped (with its failure branch) and the range fix of the existing check shipped; the checker rule stays open, as the paragraph above records.
On 2026-10-15 the owner ruled that every open GitHub issue ships in 2.0.0 (design.md 5.98): this item moves to batch 33 (issue 35).

Owner ruling 2026-10-15 (design.md 5.118, meta-spec M12): part 2 ships exact in batch 36 - a citation a claim rests on uses a recorded form a tool fills in at report time (path, line or range, the line's text or hash), and check-report-claims compares it with HEAD; free-prose citations keep the 1.4.0 checks; the unwired batch-28 heuristic module is not wired. Batch 36 holds this item (design.md 5.102).

items.title: Lifecycle: an adversarial review gate in the design phase
body: GitHub issue #38 (owner, 2026-09-30). The batch lifecycle reviews code three times (implementer self-review, task reviewer, branch reviewer) and reviews design zero times: the Design row of the orchestrating skill asks only for a spec and the owner's approval, so the owner is the first and only adversarial check on a design decision. The issue reports from the adopter project orrery: in one batch and one spec draft, four design decisions were overturned, each refuted by a cheap check. Named causes: the controller argued before it tested, did not state the rejected option's best case, and inherited concepts unexamined.

Request, three parts. (1) A design-phase gate in the lifecycle table and the orchestrating skill: before the owner sees a spec, a fresh-context reviewer on the strongest model attacks its decisions and reruns its probes, and its findings are fixed. (2) A `spec-reviewer` agent template beside `task-reviewer` and `branch-reviewer`, and a `spec-review` deliverable kind in .claude/schemas/deliverables.json, so `houserules validate` and `houserules stats` cover it. (3) Seed rules for the design phase: a decision that rejects a library or departs from the source research or an approved spec carries a captured probe, the rejected option's best case, and a reversal condition; each supporting claim is labelled run, read, or assumed, and an assumed claim is never the sole reason for a rejection; a spec lists every concept it takes from its sources, with the source's own status and a check against the goal; every decision the owner or a reviewer overturns is a `Reversal:` ledger line, and the batch retrospective counts reversals beside rule violations.

Triage 2026-10-01: part 2 adds a deliverable kind to both parity-pinned copies of the deliverables schema, a frozen surface (houserules.1-0-surface-is-frozen): it needs an owner ruling on whether the addition is a breaking change. The gate adds a review round to the lifecycle, so its design must be weighed against HR-140 (the balancing mechanism against over-bureaucratizing). A new kit-owned template changes KIT_OWNED (houserules.readme-mirrors-kit-owned).

Ruled 2026-10-01 (design.md 5.87): the item leaves batch 28 and forms batch 29 with HR-140; the surface ruling for the `spec-review` kind and the delivery path for a seed-once schema change are decided in that batch's spec.

items.title: The kit installs into a subdirectory of a repository
body: GitHub issue #41 (external reporter, 2026-10-01). The reporter could not use houserules in one subdirectory of a large legacy monorepo: an install at the repository root required moving files that belong to other domains. Request: remove the repository-root requirement. The issue names no version, no command, and no output.

Triage 2026-10-01, reproduced with the 1.1.0 tree: in a subdirectory of a git repository, `houserules init` and `houserules init --dir .` both refuse with `<dir> is not a git repository (run git init first)`. The message is wrong for this case: the directory is inside a repository, and `git init` there would create a nested one.

Scope for the spec: every read command resolves the enclosing git top level as its root; `init` requires the target to be one; the seeded hooks, the CI workflow, and the `.claude/` directory assume the repository root. A subdirectory install changes that contract across the CLI, so it needs its own spec and an owner ruling under houserules.1-0-surface-is-frozen. The error text can be corrected on its own.
Ruled 2026-10-01 (design.md 5.87): batch 28 corrects the refusal text; the subdirectory install stays open here for its own spec.

Status after batch 28: partial. The refusal text shipped: a target inside a repository gets `<target> is inside the git repository at <top level>, not its top level; houserules installs at the repository root`, derived from the nearest ancestor that holds `.git`. The subdirectory install itself stays open for its own spec.
Owner ruling 2026-10-10 (batch-33 decision D7, design.md 5.96): the subdirectory install gets its own batch after 2.0.0 (batch 34), as a minor release under the 2.0 surface rule.
On 2026-10-15 the owner ruled that every open GitHub issue ships in 2.0.0 (design.md 5.98): this item moves to batch 33; this supersedes D7 (batch 34).

Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (design.md 5.135, meta-spec O3), delivered with this item: every command defaults to the nearest directory at or above the current directory that holds .houserules.json, no higher than the git top level, else the git top level; init --dir <subdir> installs there; .claude/ and .githooks/ live in the install root and the docs say to launch Claude Code there; houserules never sets core.hooksPath, and the docs give both activations (core.hooksPath, or a call from an existing hook manager); in a subdirectory install check-commit checks only the commits that touch the install root (staged files for the hook, each commit's changed paths for --from) and prints a count of the skipped commits.

Owner ruling 2026-10-19 (design.md 5.168), delivered with this item: one repository may hold several installs; each subdirectory install gets its own seeded CI workflow .github/workflows/knowledge-<folder>.yml at the git top level, tracked and rewritten by update through a baseline; an install at the git top level keeps knowledge.yml.

items.title: check-report-claims: a comma-list citation's later line numbers are never checked
body: Found in batch 28 task 5 (HR-141). `check_citation_lines` reads a citation such as `file.rs:23,24,41` for its first number only; the later numbers are not compared with the file's line count. Batch 28 ruled the invariant for a single line and for a range: every line number a citation names fits the file it names. The comma-list form is outside that fix, and only a Limits bullet in the module doc of crates/houserules/src/report_claims.rs names the gap.

Scope for the fix: parse each number of a comma list, compare each with the file's line count, and keep the existing finding shape. Measure the retained task reports first for how often the form occurs.

items.title: vacuous-exception-gate looks for the binary under target/debug and panics under CARGO_TARGET_DIR
body: Found by both implementer scenarios of the batch-28 eval rerun. crates/houserules/src/bin/vacuous-exception-gate.rs builds the path of the houserules binary as `<root>/target/debug/<name>`. With `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` set to a directory outside the repository, the gate panics on the missing path. Both agents worked around it with a temporary `target` symlink.

Scope for the fix: resolve the binary through the build's own target directory (cargo's `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, or the path of the running gate binary), with a named error when the binary is absent. `mise run lint` runs this gate, so the fix needs a test with the variable set.

items.title: Implementer template: the closing check-report-claims run must not redirect into its own capture
body: Found by the batch-28 eval rerun (docs-edit) and by the batch-28 task-4 implementer. The closing act tells the implementer to run `houserules check-report-claims <REPORT_FILE>` and paste its clean run as the final `tests` entry. The `tests` contract asks for a redirect to a capture file. A re-run of that entry with the same redirect truncates the capture before the checker reads it, and the checker then fails the entry on a byte mismatch. The implementers worked around it: one left the closing entry without a redirect, one re-checked into a second file.

Scope for the fix: one sentence in the closing act of template/.claude/agents/implementer.md that states the form of the final entry (no redirect, or a capture file no earlier entry names). The change needs the eval rerun (process.evals-rerun).

Added by the batch-28 branch review: the same closing sequence has a second gap. The closing act says 'Not clean: fix the report and re-run'. That fix can edit a cited sentence after the citation step ran, and no step sends the implementer back. Add one sentence: after a fix to the report, repeat the citation step, then the closing run. Both edits share one eval rerun.

items.title: Citation remedy side effects: an id active and archived at once; update without a stamp resets the id prefix
body: Found in the batch-28 branch review and its fix wave (HR-146). (1) An adopter who archived a seeded entry that a kit-owned file cites, and then follows the restore remedy of check-knowledge, gets the entry back as active while knowledge/archive/ keeps the retired copy. No gate reports the id held twice. (2) `houserules update` on an install with no `.houserules.json` stamps `idPrefix` from `--id-prefix` or `WI`; the restore remedy says 'run houserules update', so a project with its own prefix and no stamp gets `WI` unless it passes the flag. (3) For a whole deleted seeded topic file, the `overrides` way out clears the citation findings but leaves dangling `see` links, and check-knowledge stays red on those.

(4) On an install with no stamp, the `overrides` way out does not keep the entry deleted past the next `update`: no baseline records the deletion, so `update` completes the stamp and writes the entry back as active. Points 1 to 3 are stated in the doc of the lint and pinned by a test in batch 28; point 4 was measured in the scoped re-review of the branch fix wave and has neither. None is changed there. Scope for a spec: decide whether check-knowledge reports an id that is both active and archived; whether the remedy names the `--id-prefix` flag for an unstamped install; whether the deleted-topic case gets its own remedy text.

items.title: stats counts a sanctioned interim fail as a violation
body: Found in the batch-28 branch review. `houserules stats` lists a fail row that the audit carries as sanctioned (`--sanctioned <rule>=<ref>`) as a violation: crates/houserules/src/rules/stats.rs reads neither the summary's `sanctioned_fail` nor the `(sanctioned: <ref>)` mark of the row. In batch 28 the id with the highest count, process.evals-rerun with 4, is the one interim fail the spec booked, so the retrospective input over-reports.

Scope for the fix: stats reports sanctioned rows in a list of their own. That changes the output shape of a frozen command, so the item needs an owner ruling under houserules.1-0-surface-is-frozen before it is scheduled.

items.title: Template and rule riders from the batch-28 branch review
body: Deferred from batch 28 into batch 29, which redesigns the review mechanism and these same templates (HR-144, HR-140, HR-129). Template defects, each with the reviewer's fix: (1) orchestrating skill: a task that adds or tightens a check in check-knowledge, check-backlog, or audit carries a paper walk in its brief (a fresh install, an install on each released kit under the new binary, an install with kept or overridden kit-owned files), and the report states each accepted red. (2) orchestrating skill, the rule that a brief's claims are measured: a brief that dictates a message reads it once for each state that prints it; a brief that dictates an enumeration derives it from the subject, never from a file name; a brief that dictates a mechanism a reviewer proposed has run it against the reviewer's own counter-example first (eight of the 31 task-review findings of batch 28 were plan-mandated). (3) branch-reviewer template: compare BASE with the remote default branch through a read-only call; list the commits in BASE..HEAD that no task report lists and review each. (4) finishing-a-feature skill, the aggregation step: fetch first; if main moved, rebuild the branch on it before the soft reset.

Clauses the review proposes for standing entries; only the owner rules these: process.claims-match-artifacts (a fix round that re-runs or re-pins an earlier round's evidence says so; a line citation into a generated evidence file is re-derived after each regeneration); process.closure-claims-carry-enumeration (a corpus of deliverables is selected by content, never by file name; an exception list is a closure with its own script); process.gates-cover-generated-commits (a check added to a shipped gate is walked through the installed populations, and the new predicate runs over the template at each release tag); process.rulings-to-file (a brief amendment that adds or drops a test, a file, or a gate against the plan is a ruling for the spec's outcomes section); writing-style.code-comments (a comment on measured or third-party behavior names an openable source; the controller files the knowledge entry before the dispatch); writing-style.doc-comments (a new caller re-opens the callee's doc comment); process.tdd (a RED against a stub of an implementation already drafted is a `mutation` entry).

Added from the batch-30 branch review (2026-10-02), deferred because batch 30 changes nothing under template/. Clauses for the kit-shipped entry knowledge-base.state-only-the-source: a premise about a third-party platform is quoted from the page's own sentence before a brief or an entry restates it; the sweep for a corrected fact is a grep for its key nouns over the tracked tree and the batch documents, in the commit that corrects it. Clauses for standing entries, which only the owner rules: process.claims-match-artifacts (a claim about a documentation page quotes every passage of the page that bears on it, and says which one the measurement supports when two disagree; a duration is recomputed from its two timestamps before the sentence ships, a rounded word included); writing-style.code-comments (a doc comment written in a fix round is swept for the round's own vocabulary before the commit, and the fix-round dispatch names the sweep). Template defects: (1) orchestrating skill, the fix-round closing rule: say which default wins for a prose-only round that closes a finding that is critical by rule class. (2) orchestrating skill and branch-reviewer template: no text covers a branch rebuilt on a moved main (the sha map, the old history, what the reviewer checks) or a loaded template that is older than the file at HEAD. (3) task-reviewer and branch-reviewer templates: 'real severity' conflicts with 'standing rule critical' for a one-word prose mismatch; a finding whose severity comes from the rule class says so first and states the size of the repair. (4) deliverables schema and implementer template: a task report of batch 30 is 267 KB, 154 KB of it pasted output in `tests`; allowing an output file with a line count for a long output needs an owner ruling, because the schema is frozen.

items.title: No lint covers a script embedded in a workflow
body: Found in batch 28 task 7. `mise run lint` runs shellcheck over the shell files under tools/, template/tools/, and the commit-msg hooks. A `run:` block of a workflow is a shell script too, and no gate reads it: the seeded install step of template/.github/workflows/knowledge.yml (25 lines of bash) and the approve step of .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml are proven only by tests that run them against stubs.

Scope for a spec: extract each `run:` block and pass it to shellcheck in the lint task, or adopt a workflow linter after a dependency vetting. The tests' shared reader (crates/houserules/tests/workflow_reader/) already extracts a step's script.

items.title: Task reports carry generated facts, not prose claims; evidence lives in files the report links
body: Owner (2026-10-09, design.md 5.90): filed as a backlog item, not built in batch 31. The cost analysis of 2026-10-09 measured task reports growing from about 55 KB (batch 2) to 316-635 KB (batches 28 and 30). About half of all 633 review findings across 26 batch workspaces target reports, evidence files, or prose, and the three rules cited most in findings are claim rules (knowledge-base.state-only-the-source 50, process.claims-match-artifacts 35, process.closure-claims-carry-enumeration 21).

Shape for a spec: `houserules` generates the fact fields of a task report (commits, test commands with exit codes, audit rows) instead of the implementer assembling them by hand; command output goes to capture files the report cites by path and hash instead of being pasted verbatim; the free-prose fields shrink to what a reviewer needs. Fewer prose claims leave less for claim rules to check.

Surface: the change edits `.claude/schemas/deliverables.json` and its template copy, a frozen surface (houserules.1-0-surface-is-frozen): a major-version bump and an adopter migration path for existing workspaces.

items.title: Seeded topic files ship in the form emit writes, so a first update rewrites nothing
body: Found in batch 31 task 2 (live run of the adopter update path). `update` re-emits every seeded knowledge topic file through `emit`; template/knowledge/quality.json and template/knowledge/security-hygiene.json are stored compact, so the first `update` of a fresh install reformats them (76 and 96 lines of whitespace). main's 1.2.0 binary updating a fresh 1.2.0 install produces the same diff, so the noise predates batch 31.

Fix: store every seeded topic file in emit's form, and add a test that `update` right after `init` leaves the knowledge files byte-identical. This lowers the friction of every adopter update (HR-161's constraint).

items.title: Deterministic checks for six judged rules the batch-31 stats run flagged
body: Filed by the batch-31 batch-close loop (process.knowledge-earns-its-place): `houserules stats` over the five most recent workspaces (batches 24 to 30; .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-09-batch-31/stats-t4-batches-24-30.json) proposes `mechanize` without an owner gate for houserules.crash-paths-are-named (2 workspaces), houserules.task-gates-mirror-ci (2), knowledge-base.state-only-the-source (4), process.wiring-checks-run-the-resolution (3), quality.user-facing-text-is-contract (2), and writing-style.instructions-cover-the-state-space (4).

For each entry a spec decides one of two outcomes: a deterministic `check` that catches the class the findings show (task-gates-mirror-ci: compare the report's gate list with .github/workflows and mise.toml; crash-paths-are-named: a lint for unwrap/expect on the named input paths), or the owner tags the entry `ruled-keep` because the rule is judged by design, so the loop stops proposing it.

The batch-32 batch-close run (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-batch-32/stats.json, batches 27 to 32) proposed `mechanize` without an owner gate again for knowledge-base.state-only-the-source, process.wiring-checks-run-the-resolution, quality.user-facing-text-is-contract, and writing-style.instructions-cover-the-state-space; this item covers them, so no new item was filed.

items.title: stats: the budget reason covers a kept set over the budget; two text fixes
body: Deferred at the re-review cap of batch 31 task 1 (process.bounded-review-loop: re-review 2 of 2 on a full-tier task; task-1-review-r2.json in the batch-31 workspace). Reason for deferral: the cap, not a judgment that the findings are wrong.

1 (Important): the `budget` reason always ends 'Demote the others that catch the least.' With every standing entry tagged `ruled-keep` it says so while `candidates` is empty, and with more kept entries than the budget no demotion of the candidates reaches the budget (reproduced in rr2-t1-budget-reason-states.txt). Fix: when `ruled_keep` exceeds the budget, the reason says the kept entries alone exceed it and that lifting a tag is the remedy; tests pin the reason in each state.
2 (Minor): README's sample `narrow` row still prints 'minor or hit a deliverable or prose'; the binary prints 'minor or hit a deliverable'.
3 (Minor): the doc comment of `is_soft` (crates/houserules/src/rules/cost.rs) conditions the prose rule on 'a repository whose docs are its product'; the code applies it everywhere.

items.title: Batch-31 retrospective proposals that change code or the two eval-covered templates
body: From the batch-31 branch review retrospective (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-09-batch-31/branch-review.json, violated_rules). Deferred out of batch 31 because each changes executable code or the implementer or task-reviewer template, which re-opens the eval run (process.evals-rerun) for a batch already past it.

1. Generate README's sample `stats` output as a frozen slice and assert the README block equals it (quality.user-facing-text-is-contract). 2. Enable rustdoc missing_docs for the crate's public items (writing-style.doc-comments). 3. check-report-claims reads backlog items and specs: a cited workspace path exists, and a cited stats run names the file that holds its window (process.claims-match-artifacts). 4. Implementer template, TDD step: a pin of existing behavior runs at BASE first and records the passing exit beside its disclosed mutation (process.tdd). 5. Task-reviewer template: a closure probe derives from the claim's subject, and an instruction keyed to a tier, count, or version is read once per value of that field (process.closure-claims-carry-enumeration, writing-style.instructions-cover-the-state-space). 6. The finishing-a-feature skill's Finish step runs `houserules check-commit --from <merge base>` with the tree binary when the batch changes the binary, since the commit-msg hook skips the check when no houserules is on PATH (batch-31 branch review, template defect 4, second half).

7. From the batch-32 branch review retrospective (process.tdd): the implementer template's fix-round contract gains one sentence. A test the fix round adds that passes before the fix gets a `mutation` tdd row in that round, with the mutation diff captured. The re-reviewer checks that every such test has one.

items.title: Four Minor findings left at the batch-31 fix-wave cap: the until clause, two texts, one report citation
body: Deferred at the re-review cap of batch 31's branch fix wave (process.bounded-review-loop; branch-fix-1-review-r2.json in the batch-31 workspace). Reason: the cap, not a judgment that the findings are wrong.

1. The summary-is-the-rule check's until clause stops at any period, so 'until 1.3.0 ships' escapes it; use (?:[^.;:]|\.\d){0,40} in both copies and add the phrase to the test's PHRASES. 2. The entry body and the test module doc say each word carries a bracketed letter; each branch of the pattern does. 3. The orchestrating skill tells a 1.0.0 install to delete the whole old CLAUDE.md line, which also carries the dispatch-template and Knowledge/BASE instructions; name only the sequential sentence, or point CLAUDE.md at AGENTS.md; the doc comment of orchestrating_skill_carries_the_agents_md_parallel_line_verbatim names only the AGENTS.md population. 4. The wave report's author-class walk cites a check-knowledge capture for 'init writes clean kit text'; cite r2-probe-widened-after-fix.txt.

items.title: Template defects: the implementer's self-audit file, the exit-code form, and several workspaces per batch
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Issues 5 and 10.

1. implementer.md names no file for the implementer's own audit run. The adopter's implementer wrote it to task-7-audit.json, the reviewer's AUDIT_JSON, and later to the re-review's path; `houserules stats` reads every task-*-audit*.json, so the batch record changed. The template states that the self-audit lives only in the report's self_audit and that the implementer writes no task-* file other than REPORT_FILE, as task-reviewer.md already states for the reviewer.

2. implementer.md forbids `;` and `|` in a captured command. An adopter rule prescribed `<command>; echo "EXIT=$?"`. The template states that the entry's `exit` field carries the exit status and that a command never appends an echo of it.

3. branch-reviewer.md assumes one workspace per batch. A batch that adds a second spec part-way has two. The dispatch names every workspace of the batch; the branch reviewer runs the workspace audit once per workspace and reads all of them, as `houserules stats` already does.

items.title: Standing rules that govern only the controller's acts stay out of task audits
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Issue 6.

Measured over this repository's 266 task reviews (7,806 judged rows): six kit standing rules whose subject is an act only the controller performs (process.brainstorm-first, process.backlog-drives-work, process.code-health-scan, process.model-policy, process.live-run-before-ci, process.owner-rulings-need-owner-supersession) and quality.well-maintained-libraries were judged 1,745 times in task reviews with 0 fails. Every standing rule sits in a glob-less area (global or process), so a file-pattern engagement test would remove no row.

Change: an entry tagged `controller` governs the controller's acts. A task audit (`houserules audit` with `--report`) leaves an entry tagged `controller` out of its package unless `--ids` names it, standing or not; the branch audit (`--workspace`) and a plain audit keep it. The kit tags its controller rules. In a batch without a branch review, the controller judges the controller rows of the branch-range audit before Finish. A tag is a free string of the knowledge schema: no schema change, no new flag.

items.title: A loading path for non-standing process rules
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Issue 7.

The seed gives the `process` area no file patterns, and knowledge-base.rules-need-a-loading-path names standing as the only other loading path, so an adopter's process rule ends up standing: judged in every audit and loaded in every session. 1.3.0 added citation loading, but only kit-owned skills and templates cite ids, and `update` overwrites them.

Change: name the loading paths a non-standing process rule already has. The controller reads every process entry's summary at each session start (the orchestrating skill's ritual, `houserules index --area process`); an agent receives the ids the controller puts on its `Knowledge:` line. The entry body, the orchestrating skill, and the migrating-knowledge skill state these paths and say that a process rule is standing only when every session must carry it; a rule only the controller can break also gets the `controller` tag.

items.title: Review findings name the caller their fix serves and the check that closes a Minor
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Issue 2, the part 1.3.0 left open.

A Minor asked for a hashable type that no caller hashes; its fix broke asdict and deepcopy and needed a second fix round. 1.3.0 closes a Minor-only round on a controller note, but the note's check is the controller's choice and no later step reads the closures.

Change: a finding whose fix adds a capability names the caller that needs it; without one, the implementer may contest it and the controller drops it or files it. Each Minor finding states the check that proves its fix (a command and its expected result); the controller runs that check for its verification note. The branch reviewer re-runs a sample of the controller notes. A seeded-violations expectation pins that a standing-rule slip of Minor impact is filed Minor.

items.title: Evidence by reference: a capture command, inline-output caps, and a checker that reads capture headers
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Issues 3 and 4.

Reports reached 821 KB; one live_run output held 437,126 characters. 25 findings (13 critical) concerned evidence form: retyped commands, a capture in the Windows ANSI code page, re-encoded and re-dated captures. Agents bent captures to pass check-report-claims, and reviewers filed that as fabricated evidence.

Change: `houserules capture --out <file> -- <command...>` runs the command and writes a header (the verbatim command, cwd, ISO start and end times, exit code, HEAD, a dirty flag) above UTF-8 output. Report entries cite the capture path, its hash, and a short excerpt; the deliverables schema caps inline output; check-report-claims verifies headers and hashes instead of parsing shell strings, which retires the cwd, output-filter, and encoding gaps rather than patching each. The audit's checker gaps need the adopter's minimal repros before they are filed separately. The schema cap is a constraint change: 2.0.0 under houserules.1-0-surface-is-frozen, with an adopter migration path. Absorbs HR-057 and HR-158.

items.title: Narrow process.rulings-to-file: a decision inside the spec's intent goes to the brief, not a spec amendment
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Root cause 9.

process.rulings-to-file counts every dispatch deviation from the spec as a ruling to amend in the same turn. The adopter's controller made nine plan-sync docs commits for decisions such as a status code or a tuple type.

Proposal: only a decision that changes what the spec states amends the spec; a decision inside the spec's intent is recorded in the task brief or the task report, and the branch review reads it there. The entry is standing and owner-seeded: it needs the owner's ruling before any build (process.owner-rulings-need-owner-supersession).
Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (design.md 5.147, meta-spec O13): joins batch 34 (2.0.0, batch 2 of 5); its standing-entry ruling is taken at the batch-34 spec review, with HR-153's standing clauses (D10).

items.title: The exit-code runner of the runner port, with linter recipes (was: a check type that runs a project linter)
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Issue 6, second half.

writing-style.doc-comments was judged 264 times in this repository's task reviews; the adopter's five doc-comment criticals are what a linter catches (rustdoc missing_docs, ruff D, eslint jsdoc). No check type runs a command, so a lint-backed rule stays a judged row.

Change: a knowledge check type that runs a named project command over the changed files and reads its exit status, plus recipes in the migrating-knowledge skill. A new check type changes the knowledge schema: batch 33, 2.0.0. Continues the mechanize proposals of HR-163.

Owner ruling 2026-10-15 (design.md 5.121, meta-spec M14): ships as the exit-code runner of HR-183's runner port, with migrating-knowledge recipes (rustdoc missing_docs, ruff D, eslint jsdoc). writing-style.doc-comments splits: the id keeps the presence clause (linter-backed, proven); a new judged entry holds the content and naming clauses. Acceptance: the presence rule leaves the judged set; the content rule stays judged.

items.title: check-report-claims flags evidence cited at a session scratchpad or /tmp path
body: From the batch-32 branch review retrospective (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-batch-32/branch-review.json). process.evidence-outlives-the-session failed twice in batch 32 (task 2 round 0: a docs_verified source with no capture; the ledger: a scratchpad path).

Change: a report `source`, `output`, or evidence string that names a path under the session scratchpad or /tmp is a claim mismatch unless a workspace capture is cited beside it. A knowledge check cannot read report strings today; the checker can (crates/houserules/src/report_claims.rs).

items.title: report-field checks test content, not presence: non-empty fields and knowledge_used against --ids
body: From the batch-32 branch review retrospective (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-batch-32/branch-review.json). Template defect 1, seen first by the batch-32 seeded-violations eval reviewer.

process.knowledge-first and security-hygiene.verify-current-docs pass on a field's presence: knowledge_used with one id and docs_verified: [] both pass (audit.rs report-field arm tests the field's presence only). items.title: report-field evidence names triggered and read report counts
body: From the batch-32 branch review retrospective (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-batch-32/branch-review.json). Template defect 2.

A report-field row's evidence reads 'report field <f> is set in N reports', where N counts the reports the check's `if` globs triggered, not the reports read. branch-reviewer.md tells the reviewer to compare that count with the workspace's task-*-report.json listing, so a check with a file-typed `if` (verify-current-docs: 'set in 1 reports' with two reports) reads as a mismatch when it is not. Change: the evidence says 'set in <triggered> of <read> reports', and the template sentence compares the second number. No schema change.

items.title: A Dependabot PR that falls behind main waits: the ruleset requires an up-to-date branch, and no rebase is promised
body: Found at the batch-28 rollout on PR #48 (HR-098, proof run 2). The `main` ruleset requires an up-to-date branch. A push to main while a Dependabot PR is open leaves the PR behind, and its enabled auto-merge then waits. GitHub's documentation promises an automatic Dependabot rebase only for conflicts ('Managing pull requests for dependency updates', read 2026-10-02: 'By default, Dependabot automatically rebases pull requests to resolve any conflicts'). What Dependabot did on its own after one of its PRs merged is in the last paragraph.

Evidence from this repository's PR timelines, read 2026-10-02. PR #32 was behind main from 2026-09-21. The weekly runs of 2026-09-25 and 2026-10-02 (about 03:55 UTC, Fridays) opened new PRs and did not rebase it. The run that batch 28's change of .github/dependabot.yml started did rebase behind PRs: it force-pushed PR #32 and PR #43 at 08:26 UTC on 2026-10-02. PR #43 changes only .github/workflows/ci.yml, which batch 28 did not touch, so that rebase resolved no conflict.

Owner rulings 2026-10-02 (design.md 5.89). First ruling: observe the weekly run of 2026-10-09. The controller then found the PR #32 evidence above, which it had not read before it asked, and proposed the reversal. Second ruling, which supersedes the first: design the fix now, as batch 30, before batch 29. PR #48 stays untouched and is the proof.

More evidence, read 2026-10-02 after PR #48 merged (10:39:38 UTC, see HR-098). Dependabot ran at 10:41 and force-pushed PRs #32 and #43 at 10:41:40 and 10:41:46; both then read `behind_by=0`. The three PRs change three different workflow files, so that rebase resolved no conflict. That is one observation, not a rule. The others: PR #32 (github-actions) stayed behind after PR #31 (cargo) merged on 2026-09-21; the release commit, a push by the owner, left PR #48 behind for almost two hours; the batch-28 push, which changed .github/dependabot.yml, was followed by rebases of PRs #32 and #43 two minutes later. The stall that this item fixes is the observed one: a push to main after which Dependabot does not rebase. PR #48 can no longer be the proof; the proof is the first run of the workflow that finds a behind PR with auto-merge on. Owner ruling 2026-10-02 at the branch review: the workflow skips a PR whose checks have failed at its current head (spec section 8).

Proof run, 2026-10-10 (batch 30 merged to main as df1f228, fast-forward from the CLI after the owner stored DEPENDABOT_AUTOMERGE_TOKEN in the Actions store): the dependabot-rebase run on the push of df1f228 (run 38076665153) found PR #53 (jdx/mise-action 5.0.0 to 5.1.1, a minor update, auto-merge on, approved, 14 commits behind main) and commented `@dependabot rebase` with the owner's token at 18:39:39 UTC. Dependabot force-pushed the rebased head f43470a at 18:40:33. dependabot-auto-merge (run 38076739486) enabled auto-merge again at 18:40:43. Every check passed, and PR #53 merged at 18:48:36 as d80588c, twelve seconds after it read CLEAN, with no owner action; GitHub names the owner's account as the merger because the owner's token enabled the auto-merge. The dependabot-rebase run on that push (run 38077278382) printed 'No Dependabot pull request with auto-merge is behind main and free of failed checks.' Closed with this run.

items.title: cargo-deny prints five duplicate-version warnings on every lint run
body: Found in the batch-30 task review. deny.toml sets `multiple-versions = "warn"` under `[bans]`, and `mise run lint` therefore prints five `warning[duplicate]` blocks on every run (measured 2026-10-02: base64, getrandom, syn, windows-link, windows-sys, two versions each, all transitive). A gate that always prints warnings trains readers to skip its output: a task report of batch 30 called the lint output clean. Scope for a ruling: keep the level and say so in deny.toml with the reason; or list the five as `skip` entries so that a new duplicate stands out; or set the level to `deny` after the list exists.

items.title: The seeded CI gate runs on GitLab as well as GitHub
body: Owner direction, 2026-10-10, at the batch-33 (2.0.0) preparation: the CI workflow must also suit projects that use GitLab instead of GitHub.

Today init and update write .github/workflows/knowledge.yml only when remote.origin.url contains github.com (install.rs GITHUB_HOSTED_SEED_ONCE, origin_is_github_hosted). Every other host gets a skip note, and the migrating-knowledge skill ('Generate your own CI gate') tells the adopter to write the gate by hand. The finishing-a-feature skill names only gh commands.

Change: a seeded GitLab CI gate that runs the same three steps (check-knowledge, check-backlog, audit on a merge request) and installs the stamped version; a host choice that also covers self-managed GitLab; GitLab steps in finishing-a-feature; a live proof in a real GitLab pipeline. Design: batch-33 spec, decision D11.

Dropped by the owner on 2026-10-10 (batch-33 decision D11, design.md 5.96): the current behavior is enough. On a host other than GitHub, init prints a note, and the migrating-knowledge skill says what to set up in the CI pipeline and how.

items.title: Seed knowledge-base.cite-durable-refs (issue 50)
body: GitHub issue 50 asks the kit to seed knowledge-base.cite-durable-refs. Design.md 5.88 ruled the entry not seeded; the owner superseded that on 2026-10-10 (batch-33 decision D6, design.md 5.96).
